sourceReference:
ATTACHED MANUEL ACADEMY LEARNER RESOURCE

Resource ID: ma-resource:ma-g3-arts-music-u03-l02

Lesson focus: simple rhythm patterns

Resource type: ACADEMY_ORIGINAL_MODEL

MODEL A — "Four-Step Signal," an eight-beat idea. Pulse: 1 2 3 4 | 1 2 3 4. Rhythm: TA TA TI-TI TA | rest TA TI-TI TA. Optional pitches: C D E G | rest E D C. Shape: rise for four beats, pause, then return. Perform by tapping, speaking syllables, moving a finger, or reading silently. Change one event for a short study. Use it to study simple rhythm patterns; describe evidence before judging and adapt the example rather than copying a finished work.

How to use it: Use the attached Manuel Academy resource in this package. It gives you the model, example, or help sheet needed for this task.

No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available and scores the same. Instead of performing, speaking, or recording, you may submit a written description of what you made or would make, a notated or diagrammed version, a labelled plan, or a written analysis covering the same criteria. Nothing in this task requires a working microphone, camera, or the ability to perform aloud.

remediation: Reteaching for simple rhythm patterns follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for simple rhythm patterns, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for simple rhythm patterns works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of simple rhythm patterns, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking simple rhythm patterns mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
extension: Apply simple rhythm patterns under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work. Treat this as optional depth on simple rhythm patterns rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
